---
title: "phplyr"
subtitle: "A PHP port of the Tidyverse's dplyr and tidyr."
---

phplyr is a library of functions for filtering, transforming, summarizing,
joining, and reshaping tables of data in PHP. Each function takes a table and
returns a new one, so a sequence of them reads as a pipeline from the raw data
to the result. The functions and their arguments follow R's
[dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org) and [tidyr](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org)
packages, and the test suite compares their results with R's.

## A first pipeline

The script below reads a CSV file of test scores from 250 students in 12
schools. It keeps the students who studied at least five hours, summarizes
each school, and prints the five schools with the highest average score.

To run it, create a Composer project in an empty directory and download the
data:

```bash
composer require phpstats/phplyr
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phplyr/v0.4.3/docs/data/schools.csv
```

Save the script as `first.php` in the same directory and run `php first.php`.
The "PHP 8.5+" version uses the pipe operator `|>`. The "PHP 8.3–8.4" version
is the same pipeline as a method chain and runs on PHP 8.3 and later.

{{< include examples/_first-pipeline.md >}}

## phplyr and phibble

The tables come from [phibble](https://github.com/phpstats/phibble), which
Composer installs with phplyr. phibble reads CSV files, database queries, and
PHP arrays into a typed, immutable `DataFrame`. Its methods, such as
`filter()`, `mutate()`, `groupBy()`, `summarize()`, `arrange()`, and `join()`,
are the operations every phibble table implements. They take closures,
arrays of column definitions, and phibble expressions.

phplyr is built on those methods and adds:

- dplyr's functions and arguments, including grouped window functions such as
  `lag()` and `min_rank()`, `across()`, column selectors such as
  `starts_with()`, `join_by()` conditions, and the `slice_*()` family.
- tidyr's pivoting, completing, splitting, nesting, and list-column functions.
- janitor's `clean_names()`, `remove_empty()`, `get_dupes()`, and `tabyl()`.
- Adapters that pass a table to phit's `lm()`, `glm()`, `lmer()`, and
  `glmer()`.

A phplyr pipeline runs on any phibble table: the in-memory `DataFrame`, a
database table from `Phibble\tbl()`, which runs the pipeline as SQL, and
`Phibble\Polars\PolarsTable`, which runs it in Polars through the phpolars
extension.

## Install

```bash
composer require phpstats/phplyr
```

phplyr supports PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5, and requires the mbstring and PDO
extensions. Pipelines written with the pipe operator `|>` need PHP 8.5.

The optional features are statistical models (the phit extension or
phit-polyfill), native descriptive statistics (phit), the Polars backend
(phpolars), janitor's transliteration of names (intl), and database tables (a
PDO driver).
[Installation](getting-started.qmd#installation) in Getting started describes
the requirements and each optional feature.

[Compatibility and limitations](compatibility.qmd) lists the PHP and backend
details and the dplyr features phplyr does not have.
